body:
I don't understand in what sense substring is better or worse than some other method. E.g. it's likely that the people who implemented prefix matching in some browsers thought that was better (matched native controls better, perhaps).

I think if we were to encourage variations (such as ignoring spelling or diacritics) we'd probably end up a similar situation as we already are, where we have developers and implementers complaining that their code works in browser X but not in browser Y.

But if you think that's an important avenue to allow, maybe we can add something like "Implementations may implement a looser form of substring matching, such as one allowing mispelling." Optionally we could even add "... but are encouraged to discuss such ideas with the larger community so they can be adopted across user agents."
